disagreements.topic: Blended fair value and the EV/EBITDA leg
disagreements.positions: Revised fair values are $83-86 (mean $84.3). Their P/E legs ($84-88) and FCF legs ($82-90) cluster, and they differ mainly in the EV/EBITDA leg: $73 for agent 4 (14x), $75.6 for agent 2 (15x), $77 for agent 1 (15.5x), $78 for agent 3 (15x) and $82 for agent 5.
disagreements.resolution: This is a matter of internal consistency, not a factual dispute. At 575M shares and ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt, the 18.5-19x P/E leg (~$86) implies an EV of ~$53B, or ~16-17x EBITDA of ~$3.2-3.3B. An EV/EBITDA leg at 14-15x is therefore effectively a second, harsher multiple haircut (~16-17x P/E equivalent) on top of the EPS haircuts agents already take. On a consistent ~16x the leg is ~$80-82. Agents 1, 2 and 4 are pulled down by $1-2 of blended value for this reason. I put fair value at $85, not $84.3. The ladder is unchanged because no fact changed.
disagreements.evidence: Arithmetic on the agents' own inputs: 575M shares, $3.8B net debt, FY28 EBITDA $3.1-3.25B, NTM EPS $4.50-4.75.

disagreements.positions: Agent 1 keeps $52, arguing that at 50% realized vol (agent 1's own, unsourced volatility estimate) a 30% fall is less than one annual standard deviation and the stock traded at $48.52 within the past year. Agents 2-5 use $55 (~12x FY28 consensus, plus preferred-conversion dilution below ~$62.5).
disagreements.resolution: Keep $55. The 52-week range is confirmed at $48.52-105.91, and the $48.52 low fell inside that window, during the above-seasonal run (the September quarter would be the sixth above-seasonal quarter), so it cannot be dismissed as a pre-recovery print. The case for $55 rests on valuation instead: ~12x FY28 consensus of $4.58 and convertible dilution below ~$62.5. At $55 the stock would trade at ~12x a consensus that the lean channel and GM guidance support. That price would signal the market pricing a reversal, not noise. Agent 1's argument is a stop-loss-width point, not a thesis point.
disagreements.evidence: 52-week range $48.52-105.91 (StockAnalysis quote page; still shown on 2026-10-14 while the Aug-Oct 2026 history page has no print below $68.75, so the low lies between Oct-2025 and Aug-2026); "sixth quarter above seasonal" for September 2026 (Q1 FY27 call, analyst question); convertible terms in the Q1 FY27 10-Q.

disagreements.topic: NTM EPS at the horizon and the size of the cycle haircut
disagreements.positions: NTM EPS at Sep-2027: agent 1 and agent 2 $4.50, agent 5 $4.55, agent 3 $4.70, agent 4 $4.75. Multiples are 18.5-19x.
disagreements.resolution: Left as is. All sit within ~5% of a consensus roll-forward (~$4.7-4.8) and multiply out to $84-88. Every agent now uses the same corrected facts: $4.58 FY28 consensus, ~7.5-8% tax, 575M shares and ~$3.8B net debt. The remaining spread is judgment about cycle maturity, which I cannot settle with search.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' revised files; Q1 FY27 8-K (Ex. 99.1); FY28 consensus from StockAnalysis/S&P Global (data as of 2026-09-18).

disagreements.topic: Bear weight and mid-2027 cycle peak
disagreements.positions: All agents cut the bear weight from 25% to 20-22% at $52, citing the lean channel (25 days) and flat 66-67% GM guidance into December, while keeping risk concentrated in mid-2027.
disagreements.resolution: Agreed. No new evidence since 2026-09-09 contradicts the CFO's commentary. The newest items are a digital power-monitor product launch (2026-09-24), the Hailo close (2026-09-21) and a 10-yr UST at 5.14%, which pressures multiples rather than fundamentals. The earnings date is still unconfirmed (est. ~2026-11-05).

confidence_reason: Round-2 forecasts have converged on the corrected facts (ladder medians ~$83-85, fair values $83-86). My searches found no new fact that separates them. The only change I make is to fair value, on consistency grounds, so the ladder stays at the forecasters' mean and there is no directional update to claim.
thesis_break_reason: $55 is ~12x FY28 consensus EPS ($4.58) and ~30% below spot. A close there would mean the market is pricing an outright cycle reversal: book-to-bill below 1, GM guided back toward ~60-62%, and distributor inventory rebuilding from 25 days. Below ~$62.5 the mandatory convertible also delivers more shares (up to ~29M below ~$51), adding dilution into weakness.
key_drivers: FY28 (Mar-2028) consensus EPS is $4.58 on $7.43B revenue (S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, data as of 2026-09-18). At the 2026-09-25 close of $78.69 the stock trades at ~17.2x FY28 consensus and ~19.1x NTM (estimate: half FY27 $3.65 + half FY28 $4.58 = $4.12).

Gross margin is guided flat at 66-67% into the December quarter (through-cycle model 65%). The full-quarter effect of the Aug/Sep price increase replaces the one-time September-quarter licensing and repricing gains.

The channel is lean: distributor inventory is 25 days, at the low end of its historical range (CFO, Q1 FY27 call), and management sees no significant customer stocking or inventory build (Citi TMT, 2026-09-09). Cycle risk sits in mid-2027, near the horizon, when the market prices FY29.

Deleveraging is slow: net debt was $5.09B in Jun-2026 and falls ~$250-300M a quarter (estimate; the June quarter was ~$170M) after ~$1.1B a year of common and preferred dividends, reaching ~$3.8B by Sep-2027 (5.09 - 5 x ~0.26). There are no buybacks until then.

Rates and sector multiple: the 10-yr UST is ~5.1-5.2% (5.17% Treasury close on 2026-09-25) and semis derated after the July-2026 selloff, which caps MCHP near 18.5-19x NTM. The next test is Q2 FY27 results, expected ~2026-11-05 (not yet confirmed).

fair_value.reason: P/E: 18.5-19x NTM EPS of ~$4.55-4.65 at Sep-2027 (575M shares, ~8% tax, light haircut to consensus) = ~$86. FCF yield (equity basis, FCF after interest and before the ~$111M preferred dividend, over 575M as-converted shares): ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45/0.05/0.575; 2.6/0.052/0.575), no net-debt deduction because FCF is already after interest. EV/EBITDA: harmonized at ~16x on ~$3.2B EBITDA, less $3.8B net debt, = ~$82, instead of the agents' 14-15x ($73-78), which double-counts the derating already in the P/E multiple. Weighted about 0.5/0.3/0.2, that gives ~$85, slightly above the $84.3 forecaster mean.

changes.why: The agents' EV/EBITDA legs at 14-15.5x imply only ~15-17x P/E on their own share, EBITDA and net-debt inputs, so they penalize the multiple twice; harmonizing that leg to ~16x lifts the blend by about $0.7.

Four of five agents use $55 (~12x FY28 consensus, and dilution from the convertible below ~$62.5); agent 1's $52 rests on a $48.52 52-week low that predates six above-seasonal quarters and the upward EPS revisions.

summary: After round 1's fact corrections the five forecasts converged tightly: fair values $83-86, ladder medians ~$83-85, all using $4.58 FY28 consensus, ~7.5-8% tax, 575M shares and ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt. New searches found nothing that changes the fundamentals. The latest news is a product launch, the Hailo close and a 10-yr UST at 5.14%, so I keep the forecasters' mean ladder (P(>= $79) ~0.56, median ~$84) and put fair value at $85, ~8% above spot plus a ~2.3% dividend. The main risk is an upcycle that peaks around mid-2027, just before the horizon, together with high rates capping semis multiples. The next checkpoint is Q2 FY27 results around early November.
